summary: The best opportunity in this batch is retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg in the TRANSCEND-T2D-2 trial. Lilly first published the topline results on Oct 28 at 10:45 UTC, so they're still inside the 48 h window. It's a randomized Phase 3 head-to-head with a semaglutide arm, which makes it the closest match yet to the EloraTZP format that qualifies for Lane C. Verified numbers (80 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes): A1C fell an average of 2.2 points on both retatrutide doses vs 1.8 on semaglutide 2 mg. Weight fell 19.5% on 9 mg and 20.9% on 12 mg vs 9.4% on semaglutide. These are company topline results and not yet peer-reviewed. Mainstream outlets (Reuters, ABC, STAT, NY Post) covered it within hours, so it's rising toward its peak. The window for the long-form is today or tomorrow, and a "what the trial actually found" angle can stand out from the "double Ozempic" headlines. Everything else feeds the playbook's Lane A queue with fresh, dated hooks: bones and muscle; stopping (the Metabolites review plus CBC); a tirzepatide plateau refreshed by a new 12-month real-world paper (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 28); and hair loss. The strongest body-worry Short hooks are the tirzepatide gallbladder and pancreas scoping review (Oct 23) and the Penn JAMA Netw Open Reddit study on gray-market retatrutide, which needs strict framing. For Instagram, the best calm benefit and body questions are menopause hormone therapy with GLP-1 weight loss, food noise with a Halloween hook, and heart benefits by age. Rejected: compounded or online-purchase content, celebrity weight-loss hype as a long-form, and observational surgery-vs-drug angles, which the playbook bans.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg (Ozempic) head-to-head: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 Phase 3, 80 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes. A1C −2.2 points on both retatrutide doses vs −1.8; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4% (Lilly topline, Oct 28, 2026)
candidates.angle: LANE C long-form, published today (inside the 48 h window). Title idea: 'Retatrutide vs Semaglutide: What the Trial Found'. Open on 'You have type 2 diabetes and you're wondering whether the next drug is really twice as strong', then answer it right away. Separate the headline from the details: the population was type 2 diabetes only; doses were 9 and 12 mg; the comparator was semaglutide's highest approved dose; these are company topline results, not yet peer-reviewed; and retatrutide is not approved. Re-hook with the blood pressure and cholesterol secondary results and with what we don't know yet (side effects in detail, the publication). Pair it with the 13:00 retatrutide Short using a loop ending. Never name dosing as advice. Say 'not approved; talk to your doctor or prescriber about what's right for you'.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–5 days (news peak Oct 28–30; search tail for weeks as creators react)
candidates.why_now: Lilly's press release went out Oct 28 at 10:45 UTC. Within 24 h it had been picked up by Reuters, STAT, ABC, NY Post, Fierce, BioSpace, HCPLive, AJMC and Everyday Health. It's the first randomized Phase 3 head-to-head between retatrutide and another incretin drug, it has a semaglutide arm, and it's well inside the 48 h freshness rule. Retatrutide Shorts are already our highest peaks (268 and 200 views).
